bark_uv_bands: bark sets are 1024x2048 with three V bands: 0-0.25 trunk base (moss/soil, not tiling in V), 0.25-0.75 trunk body, 0.75-1 limb bark; meshes split UVs at band repeats so V never leaves 0-1; U runs 0-1 around a limb and 0-2 around the thick broadleaf trunks, so the texture address mode must be WRAP in U (V can be clamp or wrap)

wind_vertex_colour.R: trunk sway weight, linear in height (0 ground, 1 top)
wind_vertex_colour.B: leaf flutter weight (0 at twig attach / wood, 1 at free card edge or blade tip)
wind_vertex_colour.A: branch bend weight (0 at trunk, 1 at limb tip); 0 on ground cover

card_normals: card vertex normals are bent toward the outward direction from the crown centre (custom split normals in the FBX); import with normals = Import, do not recompute
alpha: BC alpha is coverage with colour dilated past the edge; use masked with opacity clip about 0.33 (pine needles tolerate 0.25)

assets.name: SM_Veg_Pine_Large_01
assets.material_exception: new foliage library materials MI_Veg_* (per-species bark bands and rendered leaf/needle atlases); the shared library had only MI_Stonebrook_OakLeaf / Oak timber, which is what made every tree read as the same stylised oak
known_weaknesses: 24.2k triangles at LOD0 (cap 25k): no budget left for more spray cards; LOD1 12.8k

needle atlas v4 (12 Nov): thin pinnate branchlets with comb rows of 16-18 mm needles and open sky between side twigs; alpha coverage per tile 0.31 / 0.39 (dense tips), 0.26-0.29 (open, young), 0.13-0.16 (narrow hanging, old, half dead); cards up to 60 cm, crossed in pairs, hanging twigs, sprays laid along the boughs. Within 2-3 m a spray is still a flat plane and reads fern- or cedar-like, and needles are drawn at 3 mm pitch, coarser than a real spruce

live boughs are now 5-10 cm thick (were up to 15 cm), but the inner third of each is still bare and rather straight, and the whorls are regular: from 20 m the tiers and bare boughs show as a ladder against the sky, and the crown is open rather than full
at distance the look depends on alpha-coverage-preserving mips (clip 0.25-0.33): with plain averaged mips the fronds will either fill in to blobs or vanish; untested in Unreal
it follows the sprite's full-skirted cone, so it reads as a spruce/fir-type conifer more than a long-trunked Scots pine
bark is a tiling scan in bands (no unique bake): knots are low geometric swellings without their own bark pattern; collars are a radius swell only
buttress roots are one surface with the bole and dive 0.18 m below the pivot, but the root ridges are smooth lobes and the thin root ends are tubes whose start is hidden inside the ridge
base soil/moss darkening is delivered as a UV-channel mask (UVMask.u) and a preview blend, not baked: the Unreal bark material has to use it
LOD0 is over the 8,000 soft target
wind colours, UVMask and custom normals are untested in Unreal

known_weaknesses: v3 (12 Nov): 10-16 stems from a common stool, branches and twigs; every spray is a group of four small cards (0.15-0.3 m) at different depths, dark tiles inside and underneath, bare dead stems, gaps, long shoots; 3.5k-6.8k triangles at LOD0. The outline is ragged and sprawling rather than the sprite's round clipped bush
cards seen end-on still show as thin slivers or streaks in places; a few sunlit cards read as flat discs from the game camera
leaves are small (2.5-3 cm) because the 0.5 m spray tiles are used on small cards; the lobed leaf is a flat, evenly green scan and reads slightly graphic up close
dead stems arch low and one can lie across the ground in front of the bush (Wide); dead-twig cards at the foot read as flat brown fans from close
stems are 4-sided, branches 3-sided tubes with the dark bark set; no leaf litter or grass at the foot
two leaf types: ovate (LeafSet022) on Small and Round_Large, three-lobed (LeafSet029) on Round_Medium and Wide
new material MI_Veg_Shrub (T_Veg_Shrub_*) replaces MI_Veg_Understory on the four bushes and has to exist engine-side
wind colours and custom normals untested in Unreal

thin blades (2-6 mm = 2.5-8 texels) depend on alpha-coverage-preserving mips; untested in Unreal
new material MI_Veg_MeadowGrass has to be created engine-side; wind colours untested in Unreal

Instance it on grass terrain with random yaw and uniform scale 0.8-1.25 at about 0.5 m spacing with 0.2 m jitter (roots fill a 0.6-0.68 m square, the leaning tips overhang to about 1.2-1.4 m, so neighbours interlock); no collision; LOD2 is two crossed quads for the far field; grazed turf 6-12 cm for yards, path edges and pasture
known_weaknesses: single-quad cards 8-14 cm tall: from straight above the turf is mostly the terrain texture showing through
alpha cards carrying modelled blades (rendered atlas), not blade geometry: under about 1 m, blades in one card are coplanar and a card's bend line can show as a node across all its blades
blades are modelled (creased strips, vertex-colour gradient), not scanned; no clover, flowers or other herbs in the atlas
card normals point up so a carpet lights evenly: no per-blade specular glint
thin blades (2-6 mm = 2.5-8 texels) depend on alpha-coverage-preserving mips; untested in Unreal
new material MI_Veg_MeadowGrass has to be created engine-side; wind colours untested in Unreal
